problem: Which of the following functions is continuous on the interval $[2,\infty )?$ You may assume that all points of discontinuity for each function are shown.

examples.problem:
Determine the intervals in which the function $y= f(x)$ below is continuous. You may assume that all points of discontinuity of $f(x)$ are shown in the diagram.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13945275/assets/8281f79b06b2fa551d1a0a11135d749ba3bfbee0127c677288e90991b9aebf78.png)
examples.worked_solution:
The function is continuous on the open intervals $(-\infty,-1),$ $(-1,1)$ and $(1,\infty).$

Additionally, the function is right-continuous at $x=-1.$ Hence, it is continuous on the interval $[-1,1).$

Therefore, we can say that the function is continuous on the intervals $(-\infty,-1),$ $[-1,1)$ and $(1,\infty).$ It is also continuous on any subinterval of these intervals.

On which of the following intervals is the function $y=f(x)$ above continuous?
feedback.worked_solution:
The function is continuous on the open intervals $(-2,1),$ $(1,3)$ and $(3,\infty ).$

Additionally, the function is right-continuous at $x=-2$ and left-continuous at $x=1.$ Hence, it is continuous on the closed interval $[-2,1].$

Therefore, we can say that the function is continuous on the intervals $[-2,1]$ $(1,3)$ and $(3,\infty ).$ It is also continuous on any subinterval of these intervals.

Among the answer choices, the correct one is the following:

$\,$ $[-2,1]$ 

Notice that:

- $[-2,2]$ and $[0,2]$ contain the point $x=1,$ but the function is not right-continuous at this point.

- $[2,3]$ and $[2,4]$ contain the point $x=3$ at which the function is not defined, so the function is not continuous on these intervals.
